summary: The comparison holds up: chunk320's 19.49 us and master's 22.40 us are the same judged shape on the same evaluator, GPU and SGLang baseline, and both cover the whole full decode_1 path. The two sources touch disjoint shapes and kernels, so one scored run can confirm or refute the conjecture row by row. The import budget is safe at about 535 s of the 900 s run, but the 420 s skip threshold is too permissive and should be tightened.
justification: Like-for-like check. chunk320 job 8d4771feca9b4e18 and master job 252abb7f11ec48c3 both time the shape key 'batch=1 ctx=80000 dist=coherent heads=tp8 layer=full load=decode_1 page=1' on H200 with the same evaluator_sha256 (1d519ebf2014...) and the same baseline/reference/task hashes. SGLang's baseline on that row is 31.26 vs 31.20 us (0.2% apart), so absolute us are comparable. The paired speedups (1.604 vs 1.393) give the same ratio of 0.868. Seeds differ, but at B=1 the context is fixed at 80000, so the seed changes only values, not work. Both runs measure the full path. chunk320's top_kernels are splitkv_attn_kernel<320> 11.0 + splitkv_combine_kernel<320,16> 4.5 (the combine does v_scale, RMSNorm and sigmoid(gate), bf16 out) + _pre_attention_kernel 1.4, which is 100.0% of the profiled time. Master's are splitkv_attn_sk_kernel<4,...> 19.0 (in-kernel ticket combine and norm-gate) + _pre_attention_kernel 1.4, also 100%. Neither has a hidden FA3, gate or epilogue launch. Each row has about 2-2.6 us of inter-launch gap; chunk320 has three launches against master's two, which the 19.49 us already includes. Master's row is stable run to run (22.40 in 252abb7f, 22.53 in 917a9689), so a -2.9 us move is well outside per-shape noise (err_ns about 50). Mechanism: at B=1 x 80000 tokens, 320-token items give about 250 items on a 2xSM grid, which is better parallelism than master's two-level stream-K at grid SM. It sits about 4.5x above the 4.3 us floor, so the gain is not a floor artifact. Headline arithmetic is right: the decode_1 load is 46*11.9 + 16*22.4 = 905 us; -46 us is a 5.1% load gain, about +0.85% on the geomean. SV32: -1.1 us x 46 on a 6180 us load gives about +0.14%. The total of about +1% is inside the run's ±1.5% CI, so judge the conjecture from the per-shape rows, PATH CHOSEN lines and profile kernel names, not the headline. That is acceptable because the two changes act on disjoint rows. SOURCE B's downstream path at sliding verify_32 is still master's FA3 + combine, unchanged from when the tiled kernel was measured, so its 4.2 -> 2.7 us should transfer. Import budget. Master's run wall (started_at -> finished_at) was 469.6 s, including tests and timing. The chunk320 run, with a single load_inline, took about 344 s, which puts post-import evaluation at about 280 s and master's import at about 190 s. Adding about 65 s (one ~42 s build, the chunk320 log shows 'load_inline compiled in 42.0s', plus two gates) gives about 255 s of import and about 535 s in all, roughly 365 s of headroom. Weakest link: the 420 s start threshold. If import ever reached 420 s, the c320 build (which cannot be aborted mid-compile; its 120 s deadline only decides routing after the time is spent) plus about 280 s of evaluation would reach about 745-820 s. That is under 900 s but thin. Second weakest: GATE A's incumbent is a hand-assembled [pre-attn + two-level grid SM] pair rather than kernel_fn's real B=1 path. If it mis-models master, for example if _B1_PATH fell back to FA3 at import, the 0.98 gate compares against the wrong thing.
confounders: full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket (landed): it is the incumbent on the same row, and the route displaces it at B=1. The c320 path has no tickets, but master's _sk_b1_diagnostics/_rezero_tickets still run at import. The c320 phases must run after them and must not depend on _B1_PATH being True: if master's B=1 validation failed, master is FA3 (27+ us) and GATE A must compare against that, not against the two-level kernel.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv (landed, v1 module _EXT): the c320 port is a NEW module with only <320>/<320,16>, so master's <1024> v1 path is untouched. The chunk320 run's own full decode_32 loss came from templating the shared v1 kernel and cannot recur here. The FD1 route in kernel_fn should not require _EXT (a different module); if it is written as a branch inside _splitkv_gate, a v1 build failure would also silently disable c320, which is harmless but must be stated in PATH CHOSEN.

restack-sk-pseudo-cluster-plus-v3-fused-preattn (landed: PSEUDO route for sliding verify B=1, skF): SOURCE B's SV1 class feeds the pseudo route's q. The gate expects SV1 to stay master, but if it routes, the pseudo kernel's numerics see tiled q bytes. GATE B's exactness check (<=1% one-ulp E4M3 differences) covers this.

fused-preattention-triton / paired-heads-launch-cleanup (landed): SOURCE B replaces exactly this kernel's launch for routed verify classes. The PAIRED layout is used only on full verify B>1, which is expected to stay master. No confound on the rows under test.
restack-sliding-decode-sk-window-on-cluster-master (landed, last import phase _sd_setup): the added phases run after it, so they cannot perturb its gate timing. The only interaction is wall clock.
interference: No companion is needed. The two sources act on disjoint shape rows (full decode_1 vs sliding verify_16/32) through disjoint kernels, and each row has its own PATH CHOSEN line and distinctive profile kernel names (splitkv_attn_kernel<320>, _pre_attention_tiled_kernel). A gain or a loss on either row is therefore attributable from this one run. The conjecture's test of whether 0.87x survives on today's master is answered by comparing GATE A's in-process ratio with the judged row. An ab-revert would only repeat master's own 252abb7f/917a9689 rows, which already exist twice. A scored companion would cost a submit and add nothing.
rules_flags: No rule violation in the stated design: route tables are frozen at import, kernel_fn branches on config only, workspaces are torch.empty sized from page_table.shape[1] and batch (shape, not values), there are no tickets and no static pointers into state tensors, and it uses FP8 KV/q, fp32 merges and every key.

launch_attn<CHUNK> calls cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize). Make sure it runs at import (GATE A's first eager call), not first inside capture, and if it is behind a C++ static once-guard, that guard must be set before capture. Do not convert it into a per-call Python flag (standing policy: no per-call mutable state in kernel_fn).
IMPORT_T0 must be assigned at the very top of the module, before master's first load_inline, or the 420 s clock measures from the wrong origin and under-counts by ~190 s.

Tighten the skip rule. Start an added phase only if (now + that phase's deadline) <= ~480 s since IMPORT_T0, rather than 'now < 420 s'. A load_inline cannot be cancelled once it starts, and about 280 s of judge evaluation follows import, so the current rule allows ~820 s worst case against the 900 s hard limit.

The tiled Triton kernel must be JIT-compiled for every specialization that kernel_fn can launch (PAIRED x ROPE combos actually routed) during GATE B, so no compilation happens inside the judge's capture. If GATE B is skipped by the clock, no tiled class may be routed.
open_questions: GATE A's incumbent: prefer timing kernel_fn itself (route frozen off vs on, chosen once at import) for the B=1 full decode inputs over a hand-assembled [pre-attn + two-level] pair, so the 0.98 gate compares against exactly what master would run (including the FA3 fallback if _B1_PATH is False).

chunk320's combine kernel is 4.5 us at about 250 items x 16 heads, which is now a quarter of the row. If this lands, a follow-up should fuse or shorten the combine (for example an in-kernel ticket combine like s3's on the 320-token items).

SV16 is marked 'marginal' with a whole-step gate at 0.98. The c2ebf6ed shape moved the wrong way (22.67 -> 22.74), so expect it to stay master. If it routes, check the judged verify_16 sliding row against 22.83 us.
